findings.title: Invisible letters and marks still pass the check
findings.description: `isForbidden` flags only Cc, Cf, Zs, Zl, Zp and U+FFFD, so blank characters in other categories are let through. That covers U+3164 HANGUL FILLER and U+115F (Lo, both valid inside JavaScript identifiers), U+034F COMBINING GRAPHEME JOINER and the variation selectors U+FE00..FE0F / U+E0100.. (Mn), and U+2800 BRAILLE PATTERN BLANK (So). Any of these can sit raw in a `.ts` file without being noticed, and the invisible-identifier trick (two variables that look the same but differ by a Hangul filler) is not caught by the rule's stated goal, 'a character a reader cannot see is never written raw'.

findings.title: Rule tells authors to use a builder that fails for astral characters
findings.description: AGENTS.md rule 7 says forbidden characters may be 'built with `String.fromCharCode`', but `String.fromCharCode(0xE0001)` truncates to 16 bits and returns U+0001, not the astral format character. The new test itself uses `String.fromCodePoint`, so anyone following the rule's wording for an astral Cf character such as the U+E00xx tags gets a different character than they meant.

findings.title: Any file read error is reported as invalid UTF-8
findings.description: The bare `catch` around `readFileSync` and `TextDecoder.decode` turns every exception into `<file>: not valid UTF-8`. That includes EISDIR (a directory whose name ends in `.ts`), EACCES, and ENOENT from a file removed mid-walk. In those cases the failure message points the developer at encoding when the real cause is a filesystem error, and the original error is thrown away.

review_agent_comment: The detector is small and reads clearly.
